units.text: Source register

All web sources were consulted for the research cutoff of 11 September 2026. Links lead to the material used, not to a guarantee that the page or law will remain unchanged. Bracketed references in the text link here; each source title opens its linked text.

Legislation and judgments are distinguished from official guidance, policy reports, voluntary standards, and research proposals. WIPO Lex reproductions and national consolidations must be checked against later authoritative amendments when used for legal action. The book does not constitute a complete national-law audit.
[1] WIPO — Frequently asked questions: Copyright Official explanatory guidance. Foundational scope, automatic protection, economic and moral rights.
[2] WIPO — Summary of the Berne Convention Official treaty summary. National treatment, automatic protection, minimum rights, and terms.
[3] WTO — TRIPS Agreement, Part II, Sections 1 and 2 Treaty text. Articles 9–14 address copyright and related rights; Articles 15–21 address trademarks.
[4] WIPO — Summary of the WIPO Copyright Treaty Official treaty summary. Digital-environment rights, computer programs, compilations, and protective measures.
[5] WIPO — Summary of the Paris Convention Official treaty summary. National treatment, priority, industrial property, and unfair competition.
[6] WIPO — Madrid System Official procedural overview of international trademark registration through designated members. Not a worldwide unitary trademark.
[7] WIPO — Nice Classification Official classification resource for goods and services in trademark registration. Consult the edition applicable to a filing.
[8] United States Code — Title 17, Chapter 1 Statutory text, including sections 101, 102, 106, 107, and 117. Definitions, subject matter, exclusive rights, and limitations.
[9] United States Code — Title 17, Chapter 2 Statutory text, particularly sections 201–204. Ownership, physical copies, and transfers. Work-made-for-hire definitions also appear in section 101.
[10] United States Code — Title 17, Chapter 3 Statutory text. Duration, including special categories and historical rules.
[11] United States Code — Title 17, Chapter 4 Statutory text, particularly sections 408, 410, 411, and 412. Registration, litigation prerequisites, and remedial consequences.
[12] United States Code — Title 17, Chapter 5 Statutory text. Infringement, remedies, and section 512 service-provider provisions. Formal notices require jurisdiction-specific care.
[13] United States Code — Title 17, Chapter 12 Statutory text. Technological protection measures and copyright-management information; exceptions and exemptions require separate checking.

[14] US Copyright Office — Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability Official report, January 2025. Human authorship, expressive control, assistance, selection, arrangement, and modification. Agency analysis, not a new statute.

[15] US Copyright Office — Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training Pre-publication report, May 2025. Training, acquisition, fair use, outputs, licensing, and market considerations. The pre-publication status is material.

[16] US Copyright Office — Copyright and Artificial Intelligence initiative Official status and publication page consulted at the research cutoff. Part 3 was identified as pre-publication in the material retrieved.

[17] Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Inc. v. Goldsmith US Supreme Court, 598 U.S. 508 (2023), decided 18 May 2023. Opinion concerning the first fair-use factor for the particular licensing use.
[18] Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc. US Supreme Court, 593 U.S. 1 (2021), decided 5 April 2021. Particular API-code reuse held fair use, assuming copyrightability without deciding it.
[19] SAS Institute Inc. v. World Programming Ltd CJEU, C-406/10, 2 May 2012, ECLI:EU:C:2012:259. The linked material consulted is the Court’s official press summary, No. 53/12, not the full judgment.

[20] Directive 2009/24/EC — Legal protection of computer programs EU statutory text reproduced in WIPO Lex. Especially Articles 1, 5, 6, and 8. Subject matter, lawful observation, interoperability, and contractual limitations.

[21] Directive (EU) 2019/790 — Copyright in the Digital Single Market EU statutory text reproduced in WIPO Lex. Especially Articles 3, 4, and 7. Text and data mining, reservations, and mandatory limits. National implementation also matters.
[22] European Commission — AI Act, Article 53 Official presentation of general-purpose AI model provider obligations. Copyright-compliance policy, training-content summary, and specified exemptions.
[23] European Commission — General-Purpose AI Code of Practice Official explanatory resource. Voluntary compliance route published in July 2025; distinguish it from binding statutory duties.

[24] European Commission — AI regulatory framework Official implementation and regulatory overview, consulted in September 2026. Application dates and transitional provisions should be rechecked before action.

[25] Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 — European Union trade mark EU statutory text reproduced in WIPO Lex. Distinctiveness, infringement, limitations, classification, use, renewal, and territorial character.
[26] Directive 2006/116/EC — Term of protection EU term directive, as amended, reproduced in WIPO Lex. General life-plus-seventy rule and category-specific provisions.
[27] Directive (EU) 2016/943 — Trade secrets EU statutory text reproduced in WIPO Lex. Requirements for protection and distinctions between lawful and unlawful acquisition, use, and disclosure.

[28] Directive 2004/48/EC — Enforcement of intellectual property rights EU statutory text reproduced in WIPO Lex. Enforcement measures, evidence, safeguards, and proportionality; national implementation remains relevant.

[29] Romania — Law No. 8/1996 on Copyright and Related Rights Romanian consolidated text in WIPO Lex, amended through Law No. 69/2022 in the version consulted. Includes employee-software and mining provisions. Verify later amendments for transactions.

[30] Romania — Law No. 84/1998 on Trademarks and Geographical Indications Romanian text in WIPO Lex, amended through Emergency Ordinance No. 168/2022 in the version consulted. Verify current consolidation and procedure before filing or enforcement.
[31] Swiss IPI — Copyright at a glance Official national overview. Automatic protection and category-specific terms, including computer programs and photographs without individual character.
[32] Swiss IPI — Use of the trade mark Official guidance on commercial use, five consecutive years of non-use, and cancellation procedures.
[33] Swiss IPI — Trade mark protection at a glance Official overview. Registration, renewal, scope, and the need to investigate earlier rights independently.

[34] UK Government — Report on copyright and artificial intelligence Government report, 18 March 2026. Policy direction, text and data mining, and computer-generated works. Proposals and discussion are not enacted amendments.

[35] Japan Agency for Cultural Affairs — General Understanding on AI and Copyright: overview Official explanatory overview, May 2024. Article 30-4, non-enjoyment purposes, limits, and the distinction between development and use. Nonbinding interpretive guidance.
[36] USPTO — What is a trademark? Official US introductory guidance. Source identification and distinctions among different identifiers and intellectual property rights.
[37] USPTO — Strong trademarks Official US guidance on distinctiveness, including coined, arbitrary, suggestive, descriptive, and generic terms.
[38] USPTO — Likelihood of confusion Official examination guidance. Similarity of marks and relatedness of goods and services; searches must extend beyond identical wording.

[39] USPTO — Trademark refusal: title of a single creative work Official US registration guidance. Distinguishes single-work titles from qualifying series identifiers and discusses category-specific qualifications.
[40] Apache Software Foundation — Apache License, Version 2.0 Primary licence text. Permissions, redistribution conditions, notices, patent provisions, trademarks, and warranty limitations.
[41] Open Source Initiative — The MIT License Primary licence text reproduced by OSI. Permissions, preservation of notices, and disclaimers.
[42] GNU General Public License, version 3 Primary licence text reproduced by OSI. Read the complete conditions and definitions rather than relying on the book’s introductory explanation.
[43] GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 Primary licence text reproduced by OSI. Includes section 13 on remote network interaction for modified covered versions.

[44] Carlini et al. — Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models Original research, arXiv:2012.07805; 2020 preprint, revised 2021. Demonstrates extraction from the studied GPT-2 setting, not universal recoverability from every model.
[45] IETF — RFC 9309: Robots Exclusion Protocol Technical standard, September 2022. Crawler instructions are not access authorization or a security control.

[46] C2PA — Content Credentials Technical Specification, version 2.2 Primary technical specification. Signed provenance claims and trust model. A selected version, not a claim about the latest release or a legal ownership registry.

[47] W3C Community — Text and Data Mining Reservation Protocol Community group materials and protocol reports. Machine-readable reservations and licensing information; not legislation or necessarily a W3C Recommendation.

[48] Bartz v. Anthropic PBC — Order granting final approval of settlement US District Court, Northern District of California, case 24-cv-05417-AMO, document 680, 20 July 2026. Judicial order reproduced by the Association of American Publishers. A settlement, not a universal training precedent.

[49] Lee, Cooper, and Grimmelmann — Talkin’ ’Bout AI Generation Copyright and the Generative-AI Supply Chain. Original legal scholarship, arXiv:2309.08133, first submitted 2023. Analytical framework, not binding law.

[50] Wang, Deng, Chiba-Okabe, Barak, and Su — An Economic Solution to Copyright Challenges of Generative AI Original research proposal, arXiv:2404.13964, 2024. Contribution-based compensation using probabilistic and cooperative-game-theoretic methods.
[51] Creative Commons — Attribution 4.0 International Primary legal code. Permissions, attribution and other conditions, reservations of other rights, and limits of the grant.
[52] SPDX — Overview Official specification-project overview. Standardized component, licence, and related software information supports inventory and exchange, not automatic legal clearance.

[53] Dastar Corp. v. Twentieth Century Fox Film Corp. US Supreme Court, 539 U.S. 23 (2003). Judicial opinion reproduced by Cornell LII. Limits on using trademark-origin claims as a substitute for copyright in communicative content.

[54] Feist Publications, Inc. v. Rural Telephone Service Co. US Supreme Court, 499 U.S. 340 (1991). Judicial opinion reproduced by Cornell LII. Originality, facts, compilations, and the rejection of labour alone as the basis of copyright.
[55] Baker v. Selden US Supreme Court, 101 U.S. 99. Judicial opinion reproduced by Cornell LII. Copyright in an explanation does not establish exclusive rights to use the system explained.

[56] Computer Associates International, Inc. v. Altai, Inc. US Court of Appeals, Second Circuit, 982 F.2d 693 (1992). Judicial opinion reproduced by Justia. Software abstraction, filtration, and comparison.
[57] US Copyright Office — Fair Use Index Official explanatory resource and index. Contextual four-factor analysis; no universal safe percentage or fixed allowance.
[58] WIPO — Frequently asked questions: Patents Official introductory guidance. Exclusive rights, territoriality, licensing, and distinctions from copyright and secrecy.

[59] Directive 96/9/EC — Legal protection of databases EU statutory text reproduced in WIPO Lex. Original framework, including Article 7 on qualifying investment. Read with later amendments, including Directive (EU) 2019/790, source 21.
